source_title: One Nation MP rejects $200,000 staffer as Hanson accuses PM of meddling
source_excerpt:
Pauline Hanson has criticised the prime minister over "grubby" parliamentary staffing system. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts )
One Nation has accused Anthony Albanese of political meddling after one of its MPs rejected an unsolicited offer of a $200,000 staffer.
The dispute has intensified scrutiny of the prime minister's power to allocate parliamentary resources.
Pauline Hanson says the current system is "grubby" and wants an independent body to set staffing levels.
One Nation has accused Anthony Albanese of trying to use his power to set parliament staffing levels to divide the party after the prime minister offered new MP David Farley extra resources.
The Farrer MP received a letter from Mr Albanese this week authorising him to hire an additional staffer on a $200,000 salary package, an "unsolicited" offer that Mr Farley has rejected.
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has criticised the offer as an attempt by Labor to "exert undue political influence" and split her party, which is in the middle of a broader staffing dispute with Mr Albanese.
Staffing levels have emerged as a significant point of contention between some crossbenchers and Mr Albanese, who has ignored calls to increase the resources provided to some independents and One Nation.
All parliamentarians are granted five electorate officers, but the prime minister decides additional personal staff levels.
David Farley received the letter of offer from Anthony Albanese earlier this week. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts )
It is understood the extra staff position offered to Mr Farley was the same as the allocation provided to fellow One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce when he quit the Nationals and moved to the crossbench.
Both parliamentarians are in the lower house and have geographically large regional electorates.
Hanson says staffing power 'open to abuse'
In a statement today, Senator Hanson said the staff offer made to Mr Farley showed the system was "grubby".
"This is the type of politics that Australians are sick of," she said.
Senator Hanson has repeatedly asked Mr Albanese to let her hire more staff since One Nation achieved minor party status in the wake of Mr Joyce's defection.
"For months, One Nation has been fighting for fair, transparent and objective allocation of staffing for parliamentarians," she said.
Senator Hanson has called for an independent body to determine staffing levels.
"While this power has always been open to abuse, it has, in our view, been weaponised to an unprecedented extent under this Labor government and this prime minister," she said.
Senator apologises for 'clumsy' Haines comment
Earlier this week, independent West Australian senator Fatima Payman revealed she had apologised to Indi MP Helen Haines for her "clumsy wording" in relation to a staffing stoush with Labor.
During a Senate estimates hearing on Monday night, Senator Payman suggested Mr Albanese was waiting for her to suffer an attack similar to Ms Haines before he would grant extra staff.
Senator Payman refused to withdraw the comment at the time, which Special Minister of State Don Farrell described as an "outrageous statement".
But yesterday, Senator Payman confirmed she had contacted Ms Haines, who is in hospital recovering from a double amputation after an alleged attack last week, to clarify her remarks.
"I have apologised for my clumsy wording on Monday night, and I have conveyed those apologies directly to Dr Haines and her staff," Senator Payman said.
She maintained her need for additional staff, noting the "toll" on her current team.
Last month, Senator Hanson, Senator Payman and independent Fowler MP Dai Le teamed up to criticise what they described as "unfair" staffing double standards for some crossbenchers.
The trio called on Mr Albanese to provide a "fair" number of staff and later moved a motion attempting to strip him of the personal power to decide personnel allocations.
Fatima Payman, Pauline Hanson and Dai Le teamed up to criticise staffing allocations. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts )
Data from May this year showed Senator Payman was the only independent in parliament who did not have any additional personal staff allocated.
Ms Le had one extra staff member, as did independent Bradfield MP Nicolette Boele and United Australia Party senator Ralph Babet.
The remaining crossbench independents have two personal staff, except Tasmanian senator Jacqui Lambie, who has three.
The Greens, who have one MP and 10 senators, have 15 personal staff.
One Nation, which has two MPs and four senators, has five additional staff.
